metadata.revision_reason: Remove stratum disclosure and ID-order shortcut before reference adjudication.

cases.workflow: Emergency department bed-demand forecasting
cases.ai_intervention: Forecasting model predicts four-hour bed demand and displays confidence intervals to charge nurses.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure changes in boarding hours and staffing adjustments associated with forecast availability.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Forecast error below 15%; boarding-hour calculation reproduced for all eligible days; contemporaneous comparator identified.
cases.baseline_implementation: Four weeks before deployment were compared with four weeks after deployment at the same emergency department.
cases.evidence_locator: Capacity dashboard HC-ED-56 and daily staffing log HC-ED-SL-2
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recompute boarding hours from arrival, disposition, and bed-ready timestamps; staffing changes are transcribed from signed shift logs.
cases.evidence_gap: No concurrent department was enrolled, and the post period overlapped a seasonal respiratory surge and an added observation unit.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Direct pilot charges and time-sheet labor; shared data-pipeline expense allocated by scheduled job count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Observed boarding hours changed after launch, while seasonal volume and the new observation unit changed during the same interval.
cases.risk_facts: On three days forecast error exceeded 30%; charge nurses documented manual staffing judgments on those days.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Operations review HC-73 permits advisory forecasts with nurse-manager oversight; the model does not place staffing orders.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Emergency capacity council review after a comparator site is available.

cases.workflow: Vulnerability remediation guidance
cases.ai_intervention: Model maps scanner findings to asset context and drafts remediation steps for engineering teams.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce time from validated finding to remediation plan while preserving technical correctness and capturing support burden.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 1,000 findings; guidance accuracy at least 95%; median plan time reduced by one day; operational support hours reconciled.
cases.baseline_implementation: Sixteen pre-launch and twelve post-launch weekly cohorts used consistent severity and asset-eligibility definitions.
cases.evidence_locator: Vulnerability platform CY-VM-80, expert audit CY-VM-EA8, and support tickets CY-VM-ST24
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Rebuild cohort times from scanner and ticket timestamps; map support and rollback tickets using the archived asset-component table.
cases.evidence_gap: Platform-team debugging and emergency rollback effort were absent from the first cost view and require ticket-based reconstruction.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Finding-level usage and expert review time, with integration, debugging, and rollback labor valued from linked ticket hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Plan time changed after launch and expert accuracy was high, while a scanner upgrade and reconstructed support effort overlap the post period.
cases.risk_facts: Fourteen audited recommendations used an incompatible package version; engineers corrected thirteen before deployment and one rollback lasted 34 minutes.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Application security review CY-AS-84 covers advisory remediation text with engineering change controls and asset-owner sign-off.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Application security review after support and rollback costs are reconciled.

cases.workflow: Mortgage application document completeness review
cases.ai_intervention: Vision-language model flags missing or inconsistent fields before processor review.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce processor rework and applicant follow-up while measuring missed-document and false-flag effects.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 1,200 applications; rework reduced by 5%; missed required-document rate below 2%; subgroup false-flag rates reported.
cases.baseline_implementation: Applications were matched by channel, product, document count, processor tenure, and submission week.
cases.evidence_locator: Mortgage operations set FS-MO-77 and document audit FS-MO-DA6
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply the frozen match weights, rebuild rework events, and join the double-reviewed document sample and applicant contact logs.
cases.evidence_gap: A vendor portal update altered document naming during the final three weeks, and 18% of applicant contacts lack reason codes.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Per-application charges, sampled processor minutes, and portal remediation hours allocated to affected weeks.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched results show less rework, while portal changes, missing contact reasons, and subgroup variation widen the plausible effect range.
cases.risk_facts: False-flag rates were 3.8 percentage points higher for photographed documents than uploaded PDFs; processors reviewed every flag before contacting applicants.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Mortgage operations review FS-MO-91 covers completeness assistance with processor verification and monthly subgroup reporting.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Mortgage controls review after portal-period and document-format sensitivity analyses.

cases.workflow: Privileged-session anomaly investigation
cases.ai_intervention: Model summarizes command sequences and highlights deviations for privileged-access investigators.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure investigation time and finding accuracy within systems covered by employee notice and log-processing records.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 500 sessions; investigation time reduced by 7 minutes; material finding precision above 95%; system coverage documented.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible sessions from covered systems were randomized to assisted or existing review within risk tier.
cases.evidence_locator: Privileged access study CY-PA-55 and workforce counsel record CY-PA-WC6
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use archived risk-tier assignments, session logs, and independent finding audits; compare system identifiers with the counsel record annex.
cases.evidence_gap: The employee notice on file names production administration systems but does not name the acquired subsidiary's engineering environment.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Session-level compute and review time, plus matter-coded workforce privacy and security governance hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Risk-tier randomization and independent audits support the estimate for systems listed in the workforce notice.
cases.risk_facts: Six summaries characterized approved maintenance commands as anomalous; investigators cleared each after checking the change record.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Workforce notice CY-PA-WC6, dated 2026-04-08, lists production administration systems; the subsidiary engineering environment is absent from its system annex.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Workforce privacy and security review before any system-scope change.

cases.workflow: Identification of onboarding accounts needing additional customer-success outreach
cases.ai_intervention: Risk model highlights accounts and suggests approved onboarding actions based on product-use milestones
cases.outcome_contract: Measure six-month activation, support demand, retained recurring margin, and outreach labor against randomized account assignment.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Assignment is immutable, milestone and billing outcomes are linked for 210 days, and concurrent onboarding initiatives are recorded.
cases.baseline_implementation: New accounts were randomized within segment and contract-value blocks to model-guided outreach eligibility or standard onboarding.
cases.evidence_locator: customer-onboarding://risk-outreach/rct-210d-interim
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use original account assignment, join product milestones, outreach, support, and billing outcomes, and estimate intent-to-treat through each maturity cutoff.
cases.evidence_gap: Thirty-seven percent of accounts have not reached the billing-renewal observation point, and a new training webinar reached both arms unevenly.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Scoring and outreach labor are direct; shared onboarding integration is allocated by eligible accounts; governance uses recorded hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Random assignment supports comparison, while incomplete renewal maturity and uneven webinar exposure affect the current estimate.
cases.risk_facts: Customer-success managers dismissed 23 percent of highlighted accounts; outreach frequency remained within the existing onboarding calendar.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Onboarding review OB-303 dated 2025-12-20 covers internal risk flags and approved outreach actions through 2026-10-01.
cases.decision_checkpoint: The retention review is scheduled when the registered account-maturity threshold is reached.

cases.workflow: Preparation of multilingual summaries for complex billing-dispute handoffs
cases.ai_intervention: Assistant translates and structures prior contact history for bilingual resolution specialists
cases.outcome_contract: Measure resolution labor, repeat contact, and corrected billing value for randomized eligible disputes.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Assignment precedes specialist selection, all translated summaries receive bilingual review, and billing corrections link to dispute IDs.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible disputes in three language pairs were randomized to assistant availability or existing manual handoff preparation.
cases.evidence_locator: billing-care://multilingual-handoff/rct-09/final
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use original dispute assignment, join summary-open, review, contact, labor, and billing-correction records, and estimate by assignment.
cases.evidence_gap: Structured interviews on non-use cover 9 of 24 specialists with assistant access.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Translation calls and specialist review are direct; integration is allocated across eligible disputes; governance uses recorded language-review hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Dispute-level randomization supports the assignment estimate despite limited voluntary opening of the summaries.
cases.risk_facts: Bilingual reviewers corrected 6 of 97 opened summaries; no unreviewed summary was placed in a customer record.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Language services approval LS-109 dated 2026-01-18 covers three named language pairs and requires bilingual review before case-record use.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Billing operations will review the randomized estimate and the available specialist interviews.

cases.workflow: Payment dispute evidence assembly
cases.ai_intervention: Model retrieves transaction records and drafts a chronology for dispute specialists.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce evidence assembly time while maintaining submission completeness and measuring exception remediation effort.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 2,500 disputes; retrieval precision at least 96%; median assembly time reduced by 5 minutes; all support labor assigned.
cases.baseline_implementation: Fourteen weekly observations before and ten after launch used consistent dispute categories and queue definitions.
cases.evidence_locator: Disputes warehouse FS-DP-70, submission audit FS-DP-A5, and engineering ticket set FS-DP-T19
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Rebuild weekly queue outcomes from frozen tables; map ticket labor to the pilot using the attached service-component crosswalk.
cases.evidence_gap: Initial reporting omitted overnight incident response and temporary data-reconciliation labor later identified in tickets.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Metered transaction charges and observed specialist time, with ticket-coded integration and remediation hours valued at loaded rates.
cases.attribution_rationale: A stable post-launch time shift is observed, while a dispute-policy update and reconstructed incident labor affect interpretation.
cases.risk_facts: Forty-two evidence packets omitted one supporting record on first assembly; specialists added the record before external submission.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Payments data review FS-PD-53 covers internal retrieval and specialist-reviewed submissions for the listed dispute networks.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Disputes governance review after the incident-labor allocation is reconciled.

cases.workflow: Behavioral-health intake note summarization
cases.ai_intervention: Model summarizes intake forms and prior notes for therapist review before the first appointment.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure therapist preparation time and material omission frequency for adult outpatient intake summaries.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 300 reviewed intakes; preparation time reduced by 3 minutes; material omission rate below 2%; documented data-use coverage for every source system.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible adult intakes were randomly assigned to summary availability or existing preparation workflow before clinician assignment.
cases.evidence_locator: Behavioral health trial HC-BH-45, audit packet HC-BH-QA-4, and counsel memo HC-BH-L-9
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use the archived assignment seed, clinician activity events, and double-reviewed omission sample; source-system coverage is listed in the counsel memo appendix.
cases.evidence_gap: The current data-use authorization excludes substance-use-disorder notes governed by the cited consent conditions.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Direct invoices, measured therapist review time, and matter-coded legal and privacy hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Random assignment and complete activity logs support the time estimate within the adult outpatient population studied.
cases.risk_facts: Five of 362 summaries omitted a clinically material prior event; therapists identified all five during required source review.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Counsel memo HC-BH-L-9, dated 2026-06-12, covers adult outpatient records except the identified consent-governed note class; separate consent language has not been recorded for that class.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Behavioral health data-governance review before any change in source-system scope.

cases.workflow: Cloud identity alert investigation
cases.ai_intervention: Model assembles identity events and drafts an investigation timeline for security analysts.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce verified-alert investigation time while preserving escalation accuracy and evidence traceability.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 1,500 alerts; median investigation time reduced by 6 minutes; escalation recall at least 97%; source links present for every material claim.
cases.baseline_implementation: Alerts were randomly assigned within severity and business-unit blocks to assisted or existing investigation.
cases.evidence_locator: Security operations experiment CY-ID-98 and blind replay audit CY-ID-BR7
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use the archived assignment seed, case events, and blinded replay decisions; verify each timeline citation against immutable log identifiers.
cases.evidence_gap: Service-account alerts were excluded because ownership metadata was incomplete.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Alert-level model and storage metering, observed analyst time, and connector expense allocated by investigated alert volume.
cases.attribution_rationale: Blocked random assignment, immutable timestamps, and blinded replay support the time and escalation estimates.
cases.risk_facts: Twelve timelines omitted a relevant sign-in event; analysts found ten during review and the replay audit found two after closure, with no observed breach progression.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Security architecture record CY-SA-66 covers identity-log processing in the named tenant and requires analyst-controlled escalation.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Security operations review after the next blind replay sample.

cases.workflow: Scheduling predictive maintenance for long-haul tractor powertrains
cases.ai_intervention: Model estimates component-failure risk and suggests maintenance windows between planned routes
cases.outcome_contract: Measure roadside failures, maintenance expense, asset availability, and schedule disruption over eight months against matched tractors.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Vehicle matching is fixed before outcomes mature, work orders are linked, and concurrent preventive-maintenance campaigns are recorded.
cases.baseline_implementation: Three hundred model-monitored tractors were matched to 300 tractors by age, mileage, duty cycle, depot, and prior repair history.
cases.evidence_locator: fleet-reliability://powertrain/predictive-240d-interim
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use frozen vehicle pairs, join telemetry, work-order, roadside, and dispatch records, and estimate pair-adjusted cost through each tractor's observation cutoff.
cases.evidence_gap: Forty-one percent of tractors remain short of 240 days, and a fleet-wide coolant campaign changed maintenance activity after month five.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Telemetry and model cost are assigned by tractor-day; integration is amortized over eighteen months; technician review uses work-order time.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched vehicles support comparison, while incomplete observation and the coolant campaign affect timing and maintenance attribution.
cases.risk_facts: The model advanced 73 service visits; 19 inspected components required no work and 4 roadside failures occurred without a prior high-risk flag.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Fleet engineering approval FE-311 dated 2025-10-28 covers maintenance scheduling advice; certified technicians retain work-order authority.
cases.decision_checkpoint: The reliability board will review after fleet observation reaches the registered maturity threshold.

cases.workflow: Cross-border wealth advisory meeting preparation
cases.ai_intervention: Model summarizes client records and drafts discussion topics for adviser review before scheduled meetings.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure adviser preparation time and factual accuracy within jurisdictions covered by documented data-transfer conditions.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 400 meetings; preparation time reduced by 6 minutes; material error rate below 1%; jurisdiction and consent evidence linked for every record.
cases.baseline_implementation: Meetings in two covered jurisdictions were matched to standard preparation by adviser, client complexity, and meeting type.
cases.evidence_locator: Wealth workflow study FS-WM-60 and jurisdiction memo FS-WM-J11
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply the meeting match file, rebuild adviser preparation events, and verify jurisdiction coverage against the dated memo schedule.
cases.evidence_gap: The recorded transfer assessment covers two jurisdictions; client records from a third jurisdiction lack a completed assessment for this processing path.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Meeting-level platform costs, observed adviser minutes, and jurisdiction-specific legal and privacy hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched meetings and detailed activity events support the estimate for the two jurisdictions represented in the study.
cases.risk_facts: Three summaries misstated a prior allocation percentage; advisers corrected each before the meeting and no client document used the draft value.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Transfer assessment FS-WM-J11, dated 2026-05-20, covers jurisdictions A and B through 2027-05-19; no completed assessment is recorded for jurisdiction C.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Wealth data council review before any jurisdictional scope change.

cases.workflow: Recovery of high-value abandoned business-to-business shopping carts
cases.ai_intervention: Assistant summarizes cart context and drafts account-manager outreach for human approval
cases.outcome_contract: Measure recovered contribution margin and account-manager effort against randomized eligible carts.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Eligible carts are randomly assigned, approved outreach is logged, and recovered orders are linked within ninety days.
cases.baseline_implementation: High-value carts were randomized before account-manager assignment; managers could choose whether to open and use the draft in treated cases.
cases.evidence_locator: b2b-growth://cart-recovery/rct-27/final
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Join assignment, assistant-open, outreach, and invoice tables; estimate intent-to-treat and instrumented usage effects using registered scripts.
cases.evidence_gap: Qualitative reasons for non-use are available from only 28 of 61 assigned managers.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Usage and staff time are direct; integration is allocated by the pilot share of eligible carts.
cases.attribution_rationale: Random assignment supports the eligible-cart estimate despite limited voluntary use by account managers.
cases.risk_facts: All drafts required manager approval; two messages contained outdated delivery estimates and were corrected before sending.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Sales operations approval B2B-88 dated 2026-01-12 covers existing contracted accounts and requires an assigned manager to approve each message.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Account leadership will review the randomized estimate together with manager non-use interviews.

cases.workflow: Commercial loan covenant extraction
cases.ai_intervention: Document model extracts covenant terms and due dates for analyst verification before entry into the monitoring system.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce analyst extraction time and missed monitoring dates while maintaining field-level accuracy.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 1,000 agreements; field accuracy at least 97%; median handling time reduced by 8 minutes; no increase in missed due dates.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible agreements were randomly assigned by document batch to assisted or existing extraction, stratified by agreement complexity.
cases.evidence_locator: Loan operations trial FS-CL-105 and double-entry audit FS-CL-A7
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use the archived batch assignments, time events, and independently verified field file; join due-date exceptions by agreement identifier.
cases.evidence_gap: Results exclude scanned agreements below the prespecified image-quality threshold.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Document-level metering and observed analyst minutes; integration and governance costs allocated by processed agreement count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Stratified random assignment, independent field verification, and complete operational timestamps support the measured difference.
cases.risk_facts: Thirty-one of 1,146 agreements contained at least one corrected extraction; verification occurred before monitoring-system entry.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Model risk record FS-MR-214 and legal review FS-LR-88 cover analyst-assisted extraction for domestic commercial agreements through 2027-02-28.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Credit operations review after the scheduled quarterly field audit.

cases.workflow: Security awareness coaching personalization
cases.ai_intervention: Model selects brief coaching modules after simulated phishing events using employee role and error pattern.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce eight-month repeat simulation failures while measuring participation, manager reinforcement, and campaign variation.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 3,000 employees; repeat-failure reduction of 3 percentage points; completion above 70%; outcomes reported by role group.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible employees were randomized to personalized or standard modules within role and prior-failure strata.
cases.evidence_locator: Awareness experiment CY-AW-240 and campaign registry CY-AW-CR8
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use archived assignments, module events, and later simulation results; join manager campaigns and role changes from the registry.
cases.evidence_gap: Informal team coaching and external security training are not fully recorded, and employee roles changed during the eight-month interval.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Participant-level platform and content costs; shared campaign operations allocated by enrolled employee count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Random assignment supports module comparison, while the delayed behavior measure also reflects managers, campaign design, and role changes.
cases.risk_facts: Twelve employees reported that role-based examples disclosed more job context than expected; content was revised and no employment action was linked to module performance.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Workforce privacy review CY-WP-28 covers role-based module selection with aggregated manager reporting and eight-month event retention.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Security awareness council review after the eight-month simulation cohort closes.

cases.workflow: Identification of customers likely to replenish household consumables
cases.ai_intervention: Model selects replenishment reminders and suggested timing for consented channels
cases.outcome_contract: Measure six-month repeat-margin change and contact cost against randomized eligible-customer holdouts.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Holdout assignment remains intact, downstream orders are linked for 180 days, and overlapping loyalty offers are recorded.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible customers were assigned 80:20 to reminder eligibility or no reminder, stratified by category and prior purchase interval.
cases.evidence_locator: crm-experiments://replenishment/exp-442/six-month-snapshot
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use immutable assignment IDs, join consented-channel sends and six-month orders, then estimate intent-to-treat margin by original assignment.
cases.evidence_gap: Thirty-two percent of the cohort has not completed the full six-month observation window; loyalty offers reached both arms unevenly in month four.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Message and model charges are direct; shared CRM integration is allocated by campaign executions; staff and governance costs use recorded project hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Random assignment supports attribution, while incomplete maturation and uneven loyalty exposure broaden the current estimate.
cases.risk_facts: Reminder frequency was capped at two per category per month; opt-out rates were 0.7 percentage points higher in the eligible arm.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Consent review CRM-311 dated 2025-12-17 covers replenishment messages to customers with current marketing consent through 2026-09-30.
cases.decision_checkpoint: A cohort-maturity review is scheduled when at least 90 percent of assigned customers reach 180 days.

cases.workflow: Forecasting demand for limited-release collectibles before supplier commitment
cases.ai_intervention: Forecasting model combines waitlist activity, comparable launches, and social engagement into unit-demand ranges
cases.outcome_contract: Compare markdown, lost-sales, and inventory-financing outcomes with the established planner forecast across completed launches.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least twelve completed launches are observed, comparable-launch selection is documented, and forecast revisions retain timestamps.
cases.baseline_implementation: Nine model-assisted launches were matched to nine planner-led launches by category, price band, supplier lead time, and initial waitlist size.
cases.evidence_locator: planning-lab://collectibles/forecast-poc-6/interim
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recreate launch pairs from the preregistered distance rule and calculate financing, markdown, and imputed lost-sales values from frozen extracts.
cases.evidence_gap: Only nine of the planned twelve launch pairs are complete, and lost sales depend on a substitution-rate assumption ranging from 0.25 to 0.55.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Direct charges and planner hours are assigned by launch; integration is allocated evenly across the twelve planned pairs.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched comparisons are available, but the sample is incomplete and the estimated lost-sales component changes materially across documented substitution assumptions.
cases.risk_facts: Three forecasts were manually overridden after supplier capacity updates; override timestamps and reasons are retained.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Planning sandbox record PLN-54 dated 2026-01-29 covers advisory forecasts; supplier commitments remain signed by the category director.
cases.decision_checkpoint: The review occurs after the remaining three launch pairs close or the 120-day window ends.

cases.workflow: Endpoint incident case summarization
cases.ai_intervention: Model compiles endpoint telemetry into a chronological case summary for responders.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure responder documentation time and material correction frequency for endpoint cases.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 300 cases; documentation time reduced by 5 minutes; material correction rate reported against a concurrent workflow.
cases.baseline_implementation: Seventeen days before launch were compared with eighteen days after launch for one response team.
cases.evidence_locator: Incident case export CY-EP-35 and peer-review sample CY-EP-PR3
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recompute documentation intervals from case events and join peer-review corrections by case identifier.
cases.evidence_gap: No concurrent team was retained, and the post period followed a logging upgrade that reduced manual telemetry retrieval.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Direct pilot charges and case-event labor, with ingestion cost allocated by endpoint event volume.
cases.attribution_rationale: Documentation time declined after launch, while improved telemetry retrieval began during the same interval.
cases.risk_facts: Peer review found eight material timeline omissions among 74 sampled cases; responders amended all eight records.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Incident response record CY-IR-51 covers internal endpoint telemetry summarization with responder verification and standard evidence retention.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Incident response review after a concurrent comparison can be scheduled.

cases.workflow: Treasury cash-position narrative generation
cases.ai_intervention: Model converts intraday cash movements into a draft variance narrative for treasury analysts.
cases.outcome_contract: Measure analyst preparation time and correction frequency for daily cash-position narratives.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Thirty reporting days; narrative completion time reduced by 10 minutes; material correction count reported against a contemporaneous comparison.
cases.baseline_implementation: Twenty-one reporting days before launch were compared with twenty-one reporting days after launch in one treasury desk.
cases.evidence_locator: Treasury workflow log FS-TR-42 and controller review sheet FS-TR-C4
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recreate preparation intervals from workflow events and match corrections to the controller review sheet by reporting date.
cases.evidence_gap: The post period coincided with quarter-end process simplification, and no comparable desk retained the prior workflow.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Direct usage charges and workflow-event labor; data integration allocated by scheduled feed count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Preparation time declined after launch, but the reporting template and approval sequence also changed at quarter end.
cases.risk_facts: Controllers identified four material narrative errors in 21 post-launch reports; all were corrected before internal distribution.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Treasury technology review FS-TT-31 covers internal narrative drafting from existing cash feeds with controller sign-off.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Treasury controls review after a comparable reporting process is identified.

cases.workflow: Recognition of damaged freight from cross-dock inspection images
cases.ai_intervention: Vision model flags likely package damage and presents regions of interest to inspectors
cases.outcome_contract: Measure missed-damage claims, inspection time, secondary inspection, and full image-pipeline cost against manual inspection.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Audited recall is at least 0.9, claims are linked to inspection images, and image storage and relabeling labor are included.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eight docks transitioned in randomized waves; docks awaiting transition continued visual inspection without model flags.
cases.evidence_locator: freight-quality://damage-vision/wedge-2026Q2
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recreate dock-week exposure, join inspection, claim, storage, and label-correction logs, and apply the registered mixed-effects model.
cases.evidence_gap: Legacy image-retention costs for two docks were allocated from storage volume because the billing tags were introduced mid-study.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Inference is direct; image storage is allocated by terabyte-days; inspector and relabeling labor use shift and task logs; integration is amortized by dock-week.
cases.attribution_rationale: Randomized transition supports the operational comparison; incomplete legacy storage tags add cost uncertainty.
cases.risk_facts: Audited recall was 0.95 and precision 0.87; inspectors reopened 214 false alerts and 6 damaged parcels were missed.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Facility imaging notice FQ-45 dated 2026-02-10 covers package-only camera zones and a ninety-day retention schedule.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Quality engineering and storage finance will review claim linkage and the reconstructed storage allocation.

cases.workflow: Automated transcription and after-call summary for technical support calls
cases.ai_intervention: Speech and language models transcribe calls and draft structured disposition notes for agent confirmation
cases.outcome_contract: Measure after-call work, correction effort, downstream case quality, storage, and full transcription cost against manual notes.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Audited field accuracy is at least 0.88, agent corrections are retained, and audio storage and quality-review costs are allocated.
cases.baseline_implementation: Seven support groups transitioned in randomized weekly waves while groups awaiting rollout used manual notes.
cases.evidence_locator: contact-center://after-call-summary/wedge-77d
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recreate group-week exposure, join telephony, correction, case-reopen, storage, and review logs, and run the registered hierarchical model.
cases.evidence_gap: Supervisor quality-review time for the first two rollout weeks was reconstructed from schedule blocks rather than item-level logs.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Transcription is allocated by audio minute; storage by gigabyte-day; agent corrections and supervisor review use task logs and schedule reconstruction; integration is amortized by group-week.
cases.attribution_rationale: Randomized rollout supports comparison, while reconstructed early review labor affects the cost boundary.
cases.risk_facts: Audited structured-field accuracy was 0.94; agents corrected 8.6 percent of summaries and 0.3 percent contained another product name.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Contact recording notice CR-55 dated 2025-11-30 covers transcription and ninety-day audio retention for the seven named groups.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Operations and finance will reconcile reconstructed supervisor time and ongoing audio retention cost.

cases.workflow: Primary-care portal message drafting
cases.ai_intervention: Model proposes replies to routine portal messages for clinician editing and signature.
cases.outcome_contract: Lower clinician handling time per resolved message without increasing repeat contacts or escalation workload.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 10,000 messages; adjusted handling time reduced by 45 seconds; repeat-contact rate change within 1 percentage point.
cases.baseline_implementation: Enabled clinics were matched to non-enabled clinics on panel size, message mix, staffing, and prior response time.
cases.evidence_locator: Portal event mart HC-PM-90 and finance workpaper HC-PM-COST-3
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply the registered message exclusions, match clinics using the archived propensity scores, and recompute labor minutes from event timestamps.
cases.evidence_gap: Patient time spent composing follow-up messages was not measured.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Usage-metered platform charges and sampled clinician edit time, with shared services allocated by message count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Concurrent matching addresses measured clinic differences; repeat-contact and escalation logs capture offsetting workload.
cases.risk_facts: Among 18,420 signed replies, 63 required same-day correction and 14 led to nurse escalation; no documented injury was identified in the review window.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Clinical communications review HC-58 permits drafted replies with clinician signature and monthly exception sampling through 2026-10-15.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Ambulatory operations review at the next quarterly capacity meeting.

cases.workflow: Creation of short product-description variants for marketplace listings
cases.ai_intervention: Assistant drafts listing copy from approved catalog attributes for editor selection
cases.outcome_contract: Measure editor labor, correction time, and attributed contribution margin relative to the established template workflow.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 85 percent of eligible listings enter the assistant workflow, correction time is captured, and marketplace margin is reconciled by listing cohort.
cases.baseline_implementation: Six merchandising teams entered the workflow in randomized two-week waves while teams awaiting rollout retained the template process.

cases.workflow: Prioritization of unresolved customer complaints for specialist callbacks

cases.workflow: Preparation of account context before complex subscription-renewal calls

cases.workflow: Radiology prior-study retrieval and summary

cases.workflow: Diabetes outreach prioritization

cases.workflow: Hospital discharge medication reconciliation

cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 90 percent of eligible parcels receive estimates, scan latency is monitored, and customer contacts are linked by parcel identifier.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible parcels were randomly assigned to model-generated or rules-generated arrival windows within route-day blocks.
cases.evidence_locator: lastmile-analytics://eta-model/rct-2026-07
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Recreate route-day assignment, join scan, notification, contact, and redelivery tables, and apply finance-approved unit costs.
cases.evidence_gap: Customer satisfaction survey responses cover 11 percent of delivered parcels.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Inference and messaging charges are direct; shared event-stream expense is allocated by parcel events; staff cost uses recorded hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Route-day randomization and complete parcel linkage support the comparison; survey coverage affects only the satisfaction measure.
cases.risk_facts: Window coverage was 96 percent; 1.9 percent of model notices narrowed the window before a later delay widened it again.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Customer notification approval LM-990 dated 2025-12-09 covers estimate updates derived from operational scans and limits messages to three per parcel-day.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Product and network finance will examine the randomized outcome and recurring inference allocation.

cases.workflow: Phishing-report triage and response drafting
cases.ai_intervention: Model classifies employee-reported messages and drafts a response for analyst review.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce triage handling time while measuring false classification, analyst correction, and repeat-report workload.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 20,000 reports; handling time reduced by 30 seconds; malicious-message recall at least 99%; correction workload included.
cases.baseline_implementation: Enabled queues were matched to standard queues by report source, message type, shift, and preceding weekly volume.
cases.evidence_locator: Phishing workflow mart CY-PH-91 and red-team audit CY-PH-RT10
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply the queue match, rebuild handling events, and join analyst corrections, repeat reports, and seeded red-team messages.
cases.evidence_gap: Employee time spent reading automated responses was not measured.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Per-report metering, sampled analyst edit minutes, and shared connector and monitoring costs allocated by report count.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched queues and seeded-message audits measure time savings together with correction and repeat-report burden.
cases.risk_facts: The model initially classified 22 seeded malicious messages as benign; analyst controls intercepted 20 and delayed escalation occurred for two by under 15 minutes.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Security communications record CY-SC-39 covers message-content analysis and analyst-reviewed employee replies with 90-day content retention.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Detection engineering review at the quarterly control assessment.

cases.workflow: Dynamic selection of driving routes for hazardous-material shipments
cases.ai_intervention: Route model proposes travel paths using traffic, weather, vehicle limits, and restricted-zone data
cases.outcome_contract: Compare travel time, fuel, route deviations, and safety events with dispatcher-selected routes inside documented route conditions.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Eligible shipments are defined in advance, route versions are archived, dispatcher overrides are logged, and jurisdictional conditions are linked.
cases.baseline_implementation: Pilot shipments were matched to dispatcher-routed shipments by material class, origin-destination pair, departure band, and vehicle type.
cases.evidence_locator: hazmat-routing://pilot-hm17/audit-2026-05
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply the frozen shipment pairs, replay archived route versions, and join fuel, travel, deviation, incident, and override records.
cases.evidence_gap: The study includes only two jurisdictions and excludes severe-weather dispatches.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Routing queries and dispatcher labor are direct; integration is allocated by shipment; jurisdictional review uses recorded counsel and safety hours.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched shipments and route replay support comparison within the two included jurisdictions.
cases.risk_facts: Dispatchers overrode 16 of 204 proposals; two archived proposals crossed a newly designated local restriction before the map feed refreshed.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Safety variance HM-17 dated 2026-02-14 covers advisory routing in Jurisdictions A and B through 2026-06-30; severe-weather and Class 1 loads are outside its scope.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Safety and dispatch leaders will review jurisdiction scope, map-feed latency, and measured route outcomes.

cases.workflow: Forecasting inbound support demand for weekend staffing decisions
cases.ai_intervention: Forecasting model combines release calendars, incident signals, seasonality, and queue history into half-hour demand ranges
cases.outcome_contract: Compare staffing variance, wait time, abandonment, overtime, and forecast effort against workforce-planner forecasts.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least twelve weekends are observed, forecast versions are timestamped before schedule lock, and incident-driven adjustments are documented.
cases.baseline_implementation: Weekend outcomes cover six pre-launch and six post-launch weekends, with release volume and incident minutes included as covariates.
cases.evidence_locator: workforce-planning://weekend-forecast/poc-12w
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Use forecast versions saved before schedule lock, aggregate staffing and queue outcomes by half-hour, and fit the registered segmented model.
cases.evidence_gap: Two post-launch weekends had major incidents outside the historical range, and overtime valuation depends on whether standby payments are treated as fixed or incremental.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Forecast runs and planner hours are direct; integration is allocated by the twelve measured weekends; overtime is shown under both documented valuation treatments.
cases.attribution_rationale: The registered model adjusts for measured incident minutes, but two incidents lie outside the pre-period support and cost treatment varies by accounting assumption.
cases.risk_facts: Three half-hour intervals were understaffed by more than 20 percent during incident weekends; emergency staffing procedures were used.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Workforce planning record WP-61 dated 2026-02-07 covers advisory forecasts; schedule approval remains with the weekend operations manager.
cases.decision_checkpoint: The workforce council will review both overtime-cost treatments and incident sensitivity results.

cases.workflow: Third-party security questionnaire analysis
cases.ai_intervention: Model extracts control claims from vendor questionnaires and highlights missing supporting evidence for assessor review.
cases.outcome_contract: Reduce assessor review time while maintaining material-gap detection and documenting vendor-response variation.
cases.acceptance_criteria: At least 250 questionnaires; review time reduced by 12%; material-gap recall at least 95%; OCR and template effects reported.
cases.baseline_implementation: Assisted questionnaires were matched to standard reviews by vendor tier, template, page count, and assessor tenure.
cases.evidence_locator: Third-party risk dataset CY-TP-68 and assessor audit CY-TP-AA4
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Apply archived match weights, rebuild review intervals, and join double-scored control gaps with OCR quality measures.
cases.evidence_gap: Two major vendors changed questionnaire templates during the study, and 11% of low-quality scans lack reliable section boundaries.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Per-document platform charges, sampled assessor minutes, and OCR remediation labor allocated by affected questionnaire.
cases.attribution_rationale: Matched reviews show shorter handling time, while template changes and scan quality influence both time and detected-gap counts.
cases.risk_facts: The model missed five material control gaps in the audit sample; assessors found three during normal review and auditors found two later before contract renewal.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Third-party risk review CY-TP-72 covers questionnaire analysis within the vendor-assessment repository and requires assessor confirmation of cited evidence.
cases.decision_checkpoint: Third-party risk review after template-stratified and OCR-quality sensitivity analyses.

cases.workflow: Recovery planning after railcar connection failures at interchange yards
cases.ai_intervention: Assistant proposes feasible reblocking and onward train options for disrupted high-priority railcars
cases.outcome_contract: Measure delay-hours, demurrage, and planner labor for randomized eligible disruptions.
cases.acceptance_criteria: Disruptions are assigned before planning begins, executed plans are linked, and delay and demurrage records cover the full recovery period.
cases.baseline_implementation: Eligible high-priority disruptions were randomized to assistant availability or standard recovery planning; use remained at planner discretion.
cases.evidence_locator: rail-ops://connection-recovery/rct-14/final
cases.evidence_reproduction_note: Rebuild assignment from event IDs, join assistant access, selected recovery plan, movement, demurrage, and labor records, and estimate by assignment.
cases.evidence_gap: Non-use interviews cover 13 of 29 planners assigned access.
cases.cost_allocation_method: Model calls and planner time are direct; integration cost is allocated across randomized disruption events.
cases.attribution_rationale: Event-level randomization supports the assignment estimate despite planners opening the assistant in a minority of eligible events.
cases.risk_facts: Planners selected 38 proposed plans; one selected plan was later revised after a track-availability update.
cases.authorization_evidence_facts: Rail operations trial record RO-144 dated 2026-01-15 covers advisory plans for priority classes P1 and P2; dispatch release remains with the network controller.
cases.decision_checkpoint: The rail planning committee will review the randomized estimate and the available non-use interviews.
